status: development-only; NOT promoted; no frozen/registered model changed
objective: Use the local GPU (RTX 4060, torch 2.6.0+cu124) to test whether a neural action-conditioned JEPA can match or beat the existing non-neural world model on the incident-dynamics PHYSICAL domain. Development trial on a fresh run-id; the registered v2/v3/v4 finals and the deployed Physical JEPA v5 artifact were not touched.

result.verdict: The GPU neural JEPA is about 15x WORSE than the existing non-neural selected model on the physical domain (H5 0.0178 vs 0.00116). It does not improve the world model here.

interpretation: Confirms, now on-device, the repository's prior finding that gradient-boosted/ridge models dominate neural families on the low-dimensional (16-d) abstract simulators (work.md; incident_dynamics_result_v3/v4). The GPU and training pipeline work correctly; the neural approach simply has no structural advantage at this input dimensionality. The plausible GPU win is high-dimensional real telemetry (86-channel HAI), tested separately and forecasting-only in docs/research/real_telemetry_hai_forecast_jepa_vs_ridge.json.
caveats: Single method (action_conditioned_jepa), single seed; a wider sweep would likely still lose given the documented margin.

Validation MAE from the trainer; the v4 'selected' numbers are from the v4 harness, so the comparison is indicative of magnitude, not a like-for-like re-evaluation. The ~15x gap is far larger than any metric-convention difference.
Development only: nothing is promoted, and the deployed Physical JEPA v5 digest is verified unchanged before and after the run.
